h: מוֹצָאֵי יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים, ד׳ Motzei Yom Kippur, 4

p: 'And I will sprinkle upon you,' etc.,
For the essence of Yom Kippur
is the purification of the soul
from the filth of the leaven in the dough,
וְהִנֵּה יֵשׁ שְׁלֹשָׁה מִינֵי טוּמְאוֹת בָּעוֹלָם
Now, there are three kinds of tumah in the world,
as they are spelled out in the holy Torah
"They shall send out of the camp
and everyone made tamei by the dead."
And because there is rooted in us
the holiness of the three holy Avos,
we are able to become pure
For the metzora is one who is bad to people,
through sins between man and his fellow,
because he separated between a man and his fellow."
And because we are by birth
the seed of Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
we are able to be purified from the tumah of tzaraas,
even if it has clung to some individual
since at the root there are rooted in us
the traits of the three Avos,
comes from the side of the man of desire,
and he is sent out of the camp of the Levi'im.
Here too there is the power to become pure,
וּבְחִינַת קְדוּשַּׁת יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
through the aspect of the holiness of Yitzchak Avinu, peace be upon him,
of every kind of desire of this world,
"And he dwelt in the land of the Negev."
the expression "the land of the Negev"
"that is dried out," etc. End of the manuscript note.)
That is, his heart was dried out of all desire,
וְהוּא שׂוֹרֵף אֶת כָּל מִינֵי תַּאֲוָה שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם.
and it burns up every kind of desire in the world.
before the King of kings of kings
is seized by dread and fear,
for any desire to enter the heart.
And this is of the aspect of true yirah,
which is the aspect of the attribute of Yitzchak,
Hakadosh Baruch Hu before their eyes."
that they had the strength "to stand in the king's palace,"
meaning that they forcibly held themselves back
how much more so when one stands
לִפְנֵי מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא.
before the King of kings of kings, Hakadosh Baruch Hu.
And the tumah of the dead,
that is, one made tamei by the dead,
is when vitality is absent from him
and therefore he is sent out
of the camp of the Shechinah.
And included in the tumah of the dead
is also the tumah of a sheretz,
whose bearer is sent out only from the camp of the Shechinah;
and the tumah of a sheretz serves as the term
for all tumah in the Torah,
"like one who immerses with a sheretz in his hand."
And through the aspect of the attribute
of the holiness of Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
"The lip of truth shall be established forever,"
and there was rooted in him
all the holiness of the Torah as a whole,
כִּי הֲגַם שֶׁאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
For although Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
קִייֵּם גַּם כֵּן אֶת כָּל הַתּוֹרָה (יוֹמָא כח, ב),
of the Torah of truth forever in the heart
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהָיָה שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַחִיּוּת שֶׁל הַקְּדוּשָּׁה
because he was the root of the vitality of holiness,
And through this we are able to become pure
even from the tumah of the dead,
לִהְיוֹת דָּבוּק בְּשֹׁרֶשׁ הַחִיּוּת שֶׁל הַקְּדוּשָּׁה
to be attached to the root of the vitality of holiness
and to enter the camp of the Shechinah,
הֲגַם שֶׁאֵין לוֹ הַבְחָנָה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
even though this cannot be discerned in this world.
כִּי הֲלֹא גַּם בְּחִינַת יַעֲקֹב בְּעַצְמוֹ
For indeed even the aspect of Yaakov himself
cannot be discerned in this world,
as it says in the Gemara (ibid.):
"Was it for nothing that the embalmers embalmed him?"
just as his offspring are alive,
וְעַל זֶה מְרַמֵּז טָהֳרַת יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים
And to this the purification of Yom Kippur alludes:
in the very root of the vitality of holiness,
that one not be separated from Hashem Yisbarach,
so that he can enter the camp of the Shechinah,
"And I will sprinkle pure water upon you" —
this corresponds to the purification of one made tamei by the dead.
And it said, "The mikveh of Israel is Hashem" —
this corresponds to purification from the tumah of zivah,
הִיא עַל יְדֵי מִקְוֵה מַיִם דַּיְיקָא.
is precisely through a mikveh of water.
And the third purification, from the tumah of tzaraas,
is not alluded to in connection with Yom Kippur,
because it comes for being bad to people,
and it stems from a sin between man and his fellow,
as it says in the Gemara (Yoma 85b).
